Iran Human Rights

Mehr Qayyum

2026-01-14

Background

“Iran’s binding obligations under international human rights law, including the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR). Peaceful protest is not a security threat; it is a protected civic right. The systematic suppression of dissent—through lethal force, mass arrests, and communication blackouts— risks further loss of life and irreversible damage to the rule of law.

The National Iranian American Council strongly condemns the killing of peaceful protesters, including children, and stands in solidarity with the Iranian people against this brutal crackdown.” ~National Iranian American Council

Analyst Note: For all violation types between two affiliations: Apply Chi -Square Test: chisq.test() on a 2 × 21 table

Works fine because the table is small and not sparse

Class Notes: * Compare 2 affiliations on 1 violation type = Use Two‑proportion test * Compare 2 affiliations on all violation types = Use Small chi‑square * Compare all 43 affiliations on 1 violation type = Use Logistic regression * Compare all 43 affiliations on all violation types = Use Multinomial or log‑linear model * BUT Run 903 pairwise comparisons =Possible but not recommended BUT, If we compare all 43 affiliations simultaneously across all violation types

That’s a 43 × 21 chi‑square test, but it fails because:

too many cells and too many zeros

expected counts < 5 everywhere

df = 840

chi‑square approximation breaks

So the global chi‑square is not reliable.

iran_df
head(iran_df)
summary(iran_df) #

#Clean: treat each row as a pipe‑separated list of violation types, split them into individual entries, clean them, and #then count how often each one appears across all 947 records.

#Count Human Rights Violation Type

#split on pipe |
iran_df_long <- iran_df %>% 
  separate_rows(Violation_Type, sep = "\\|")

#Clean white space
iran_df_long  <- iran_df_long  %>% 
  mutate(Violation_Type = str_trim(Violation_Type)) %>% 
  filter(Violation_Type != "")

#Count Each violation type
violation_counts <- iran_df_long %>% count(Violation_Type, sort = TRUE)
violation_counts
#Subset to list of 10
top_10 <- violation_counts %>% slice_max(n, n = 10)

#Flag top 10 in main data frame
iran_df_long <- iran_df_long %>% mutate(is_top_10 = Violation_Type %in% top_10$Violation_Type)
#Visualize All Types in Horizontal
ggplot(violation_counts, aes(x = reorder(Violation_Type, n), y = n)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + coord_flip() + labs( title = "Counts of Violation Types", x = "Violation Type", y = "Count" ) + theme_minimal()

#Emphasize Top 10
violation_counts <- violation_counts %>% mutate(is_top_10 = Violation_Type %in% top_10$Violation_Type) %>% arrange(desc(n))
violation_counts <- violation_counts %>% mutate(Violation_Type = factor(Violation_Type, levels = unique(Violation_Type)))
top_10 <- violation_counts %>% 
 slice_max(n, n = 10)



# Add a flag 
top10_image <- ggplot(violation_counts, aes(x = Violation_Type, y = n, fill = is_top_10)) + geom_col() + scale_fill_manual( values = c("gray80", "magenta"), labels = c("Other Violations", "Top 10 Violations"), name = "Violation Category" ) + coord_flip() + labs( title = "Human Rights Violations in Iran (Top 10 Highlighted)", x = "Violation Type", y = "Count" ) + theme_minimal()

top10_image

#export image
ggsave("violations_top10.png", top10_image, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

#Does affiliation relate to violation type?

#Affiliation Note: my baseline is Judicial system of Iran
affiliation_counts <- iran_df_long %>% count(Affiliation, sort = TRUE)
affiliation_counts

#Proportion T-test on “Use of Excessive Force on Civilians” Between Top 2 Branches

target <- "Use of Excessive Force on Civilians"
iran_df_long <- iran_df_long %>% mutate(Violation_Type = str_trim(Violation_Type))

#Specify Affiliation
aff_A <- "Judicial system of Iran" #Affiliation A" 
aff_B <- "Law Enforcement Force"#"Affiliation B"

#Count How Many Types Both Affiliations Committed Same Violation for Rate
# Number of target violations by each affiliation 
x_judicial <- iran_df_long %>% filter(Affiliation == aff_A, Violation_Type == target) %>% nrow() 
x_law_enf <- iran_df_long %>% filter(Affiliation == aff_B, Violation_Type == target) %>% nrow()

#Denominator for total violations of target type by each affiliation
total_violations_by_A  <- iran_df_long %>% filter(Affiliation == "Judicial system of Iran") %>% nrow()
total_violations_by_B  <- iran_df_long %>% filter(Affiliation == "Law Enforcement Force") %>% nrow()


#Run the Proportion Test
prop.test( x = c(x_judicial, x_law_enf), n = c(total_violations_by_A, total_violations_by_B), alternative = "two.sided", correct = FALSE )
## 
##  2-sample test for equality of proportions without continuity correction
## 
## data:  c(x_judicial, x_law_enf) out of c(total_violations_by_A, total_violations_by_B)
## X-squared = 57.966, df = 1, p-value = 2.667e-14
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.07748654 -0.04365140
## sample estimates:
##     prop 1     prop 2 
## 0.02017115 0.08074012

#Visualize as Dot Plot

#Build a small table
proportion_df <- tibble( Affiliation = c("Judicial system of Iran", "Law Enforcement Force"), Count = c(x_judicial, x_law_enf), Total = c(total_violations_by_A, total_violations_by_B) ) %>% mutate(Proportion = Count / Total)

ggplot(proportion_df, aes(x = Proportion, y = Affiliation)) + geom_point(size = 5, color = "darkmagenta") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) + labs( title = "Proportion of 'Use of Excessive Force on Civilians' by Affiliation", x = "Proportion", y = "Affiliation" ) + theme_minimal()

## Analytical Interpretation Affiliation A (Judicial system of Iran): 0.02017

Affiliation B (Law Enforcement Force): 0.08074 * Affiliation B (Law enforcement) commits more of target violations “excessive force against civilians” than affiliation A (Judicial Sytem) commits. Specifically, B’s rate is about 4 times higher than judicial.

Our p-value tells us that the difference in proportions is statistically significant.

Now for same single violation, but reviewing ALL affiliations, use logistic regression (for one violation type). # Compare the distribution of all violation types across affiliations:

model_violations_iran <- nnet::multinom(Violation_Type ~ Affiliation, data = iran_df_long)

# Analysis 
Each violation type has its own coefficient (relative to a baseline category)

Each affiliation has its own coefficient (relative to a baseline affiliation)

The numbers represent log‑odds, not probabilities.
The first column is the intercept for each violation type

The second column is the coefficient for Affiliation = Appointed by Islamic Republic Supreme Leader  
(relative to the baseline affiliation, which is likely the first alphabetically or the first factor level)

So each row tells you:

How the log‑odds of a specific violation type change when the affiliation is “Appointed by Islamic Republic Supreme Leader” instead of the baseline affiliation.
~A coefficient is in log‑odds.

Positive coefficient → higher odds of that violation type for that affiliation

Negative coefficient → lower odds

Magnitude → strength of the effect

Exponentiate to get odds ratios:
exp⁡(𝛽)

So, "Use of Excessive Force on Civilians":  -1.19531465, which is exp(-1.1953)= odds ratio =0.30, so this affiliation is 70% less likely  to be associated with “Use of Excessive Force on Civilians” compared to the baseline affiliation.

Freedom of expression and thought
Coefficient: +0.9295  
Odds ratio ≈ 2.53

➡️ This affiliation is 2.5× more likely to commit this violation than the baseline.

Torture
Coefficient: +1.1658  
Odds ratio ≈ 3.21

➡️ This affiliation is over 3× more likely to be associated with torture than the baseline.
~ For the affiliation “Appointed by Islamic Republic Supreme Leader”:

They are more likely to be associated with:

Torture, Social rights violations, Freedom of expression violations, Right to Freedom, Right to Protest

But They are less likely to be associated with:

Use of Excessive Force on Civilians

LGBTQ+ rights violations

Right to health

Environment

Worker’s rights

Union’s rights

Some categories have extremely negative coefficients because they almost never occur for this affiliation.

Logistic Regression Allows all 43 Affiliations/ Entities Compared on 1 Violation Type

#Create Binary Outcome  where 1=right to protest
iran_df_protest_model <- iran_df_long %>% mutate( protest_binary = ifelse(Violation_Type == "Right to Protest", 1, 0), Affiliation = factor(Affiliation)) 
#ensure it's a factor  

protest_model <- glm( protest_binary ~ Affiliation, data = iran_df_protest_model, family = binomial )
summary(protest_model)

#Remove intercept
tidy_or <- tidy_or %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)")

#Fix Prefix
tidy_or <- tidy_or %>% mutate( Affiliation = str_remove(term, "Affiliation"), Affiliation = str_trim(Affiliation) )

#Build Forest Model
protest_forest_plot <- ggplot(tidy_or, aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(Affiliation, estimate))) + geom_point(color = "magenta", size = 3) + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) + geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") + scale_x_log10() + labs( title = "Odds Ratios for 'Right to Protest' Violations by Affiliation", x = "Odds Ratio (log scale)", y = "Affiliation" ) + theme_minimal()

protest_forest_plot
